chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

"Whoever kills a believer intentionally, then qiṣāṣ is carried out against him, unless the heirs of the slain are satisfied to accept the diyah, or they mutually agree upon more than the diyah or less than the diyah. If they do that among themselves, it is permissible; and if they do not come to a mutual agreement, qiṣāṣ is carried out."
And he said: "The diyah is ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars, or one hundred camels."

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal representatives of the slain person
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: financial blood-compensation paid in lieu of retaliation
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: dirham; a unit of silver currency used to quantify diyah
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: dinar; a unit of gold currency used to quantify diyah
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer; the protected victim mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.يَتَرَاضَوْا: they mutually agree; indicating consensual settlement
key_terms.يُقَادُ: qiṣāṣ is carried out; the killer is subjected to legal retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intentional killing and diyah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the ruling for intentional killing of a believer: the default ruling is qiṣāṣ, unless the slain person's heirs accept diyah or mutually agree on a different amount. It also specifies standard equivalents for the diyah, showing the legal framework for compensation and settlement in cases of homicide.
